summary.headline: DOMS Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 19.2% to INR670 crore, but EBITDA fell 16.4% to INR82.6 crore as margin dropped to 12.3% on raw material inflation.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 19.2% YoY to INR670 crore on volume growth, with only a calibrated price increase of about 4-5%. EBITDA margin compressed to 12.3% from 17.6%, mainly from roughly 400 bps gross margin decline due to West Asia-linked raw material inflation (about 20% average RM price rise in Q1), plus ESOP, new-facility and channel partner event costs. PAT fell to INR45.3 crore from INR59.1 crore, with PAT margin at 6.8% versus 10.5%. Management chose volume and market share over near-term margin, calls the margin dip temporary, and gave limited visibility on margins given fluctuating raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR59.1 crore in Q1 FY26 (-23% YoY)
Against about 10-11% consumption cost increase; about 500 bps left to pass on

segments.name: Scholastic stationery, scholastic art material and paper stationery
segments.commentary: Growth led by back-to-school season, new launches and recent capacity additions; no segment-level figures disclosed.

segments.name: Office supplies (pens, mechanical pencils, erasers, pencil boxes, school bags and kits)
segments.commentary: Described as high positive traction with strong acceptance of new launches; no revenue figure disclosed.

segments.name: Baby hygiene (Uniclan diapers)
segments.commentary: Drove high growth in modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce; EBITDA margin held up in Q1, but raw material (SAP, non-woven fabric) costs are expected to hit from Q2, partly offset by seasonal fixed-cost absorption.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Flattish in Q1 due to EU demand softness and West Asia logistics disruption; West Asia is about 2% of sales. Exports are about 12% of total revenue; full-year export share guided at 13-15%.

segments.name: West India region
segments.commentary: Revenue declined YoY from about INR186 crore to close to INR140 crore, mainly due to lower merchant export sales routed via western India customers.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated revenue growth guidance of 18-20% for FY27 reaffirmed, with the second-half contribution expected from the 50-plus acre greenfield plant.

Gross/EBITDA margin: management reiterated the long-term EBITDA target of about 16-17%, but gave limited visibility on margins; at current spot raw material prices, a further 4-5% price increase may be needed to return to 16-odd % margin in FY28.
Management indicated FY26 gross and EBITDA margins as the sweet spot to maintain going forward (FY28 framing), while also saying Q1 may be the margin bottom.
No further price hikes planned in Q1 FY27; decision to wait for raw material volatility to settle.
ESOP cost for FY27 from the Oct-24 and Feb-26 tranches expected at about INR10 crore for the full year; FY28 ESOP cost to rise as further grants are made.
Reynolds brand expected to contribute close to 10% of group revenue by FY29; management declined to guide FY28 revenue growth yet, saying it will do so in later calls.
Export share of revenue guided at 13-15% for full FY27.
capex_capacity: About 300,000 sq ft of operational area expected to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27 at the 50-plus acre greenfield project in Umbergaon; first building possession already taken.
Adjoining land of about 11-plus acres acquired near existing facilities in Umbergaon and Jammu, to be developed.
Capex economics: target sales-to-capex ratio of about 3x; FY26 achieved about 2.7x. Facilities take 18-24 months to reach full utilisation.
Capex of about INR200-250 crore per year cited by an analyst; management did not confirm this figure.
Reynolds: asset purchase complete, Reynolds team integrated and assets moved to the Umbergaon facility. Reynolds production to start in the first phase of the new plant, targeted for end Q2 FY27.
Swiss-imported tip manufacturing machine installation under way; targets 30-40% in-house tip requirements over the current and next calendar year.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth with domestic demand robust; strong back-to-school season.
Average price increase of 4-5% taken; industry reportedly took a similar calibrated step.
Raw material prices eased toward end-June, then rose again in the last few weeks on renewed West Asia tensions; management expects prices to cool over time.
Management chose not to take larger price hikes to protect market share and shelf space, arguing peers and unorganised players gain breathing room when leaders delay pricing.

Reynolds brand: FY26 sales about INR130-140 crore under Newell; positioned in INR10-100 pen price band, targeted at serious and professional users; may lift ASPs but not volumes, as it substitutes DOMS capacity.
Export demand soft in certain EU economies; West Asia disruptions causing longer transit, higher freight and shipment deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Why not take larger price hikes, and will margins stay weak in FY27 and normalise only in FY28? Also, how much can H2 revenue grow beyond 20%, and what is Reynolds' FY28 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised volume-led growth and market share; price increases were calibrated and raw material prices eased toward end-June before rising again in recent weeks. Margins are structurally intact with a return to the 16-17% guided range once prices stabilise. 18-20% FY27 revenue guidance reaffirmed; Reynolds adds little incremental volume as it uses diverted existing capacity, and it is expected to contribute about 10% of revenue by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material price has been passed on, how much is left, and what are the one-off costs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Average price increase taken is about 4-5% against about 20% average RM price rise in Q1, which translates to 10-11% consumption cost increase, leaving about 500 bps to pass on. ESOP added about 0.2% to cost; the channel partner event cost about 0.4% of margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Reynolds nib (OEM) business not acquired, and what is the backward integration plan for tips?
qa_highlights.answer: Newell was exiting only the Reynolds brand and related India assets and wanted to keep its tip manufacturing; the deal covered only the brand and assets. DOMS has a Swiss-imported tip plant under installation, targeting 30-40% in-house tip needs over the current and next calendar year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Uniclan's EBITDA margin intact while stationery margins fell about 600 bps, and will Q2 see further gross margin pressure from higher-cost inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Uniclan was also hit by crude-linked inputs (SAP and non-woven fabric), but its long-term contracts delayed the impact; the hit is expected in Q2. Management said DOMS carries low inventory of locally bought polymers, so no major inventory-cost effect, and Q2 seasonal fixed-cost absorption in diapers should offset part of the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why were exports flattish and why did West India revenue fall from about INR186 crore to about INR140 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were hit by EU demand softness, West Asia transit delays, higher freight and shipment deferrals; West Asia is about 2% of sales. West India fell due to lower merchant export sales via western India customers. Full-year export share guided at 13-15% (about 12% currently), helped by new pencil capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What capex-to-sales returns apply, and why not accelerate capex (for example INR400 crore over 12 months) to capture Reynolds demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Target sales-to-capex is about 3x against 2.7x achieved in FY26; facilities take 18-24 months to reach full utilisation. Management said physical space, not funding, is the constraint, with 50-plus acres under development and 11-plus acres added near Umbergaon and Jammu.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: spot prices rose again in the last few weeks on renewed West Asia tensions; a further 4-5% price hike may be needed for FY28 margins of 16-odd %.
Gross margin recovery: Uniclan raw material cost impact expected from Q2, and visibility on margins remains limited.
Execution of the 50-plus acre Umbergaon plant: about 300,000 sq ft targeted by end Q2 FY27, with H2 growth dependent on it; full utilisation takes 18-24 months.
Reynolds integration: brand contributes about 10% of revenue by FY29; the margin structure of the brand under DOMS is yet to be proven, and it substitutes DOMS capacity rather than adding volume.
Exports and West India: EU demand softness and West Asia logistics could keep exports flat; FY27 export share guided at 13-15%.
ESOP cost rising: about INR10 crore in FY27 from the Oct-24 and Feb-26 tranches, with FY28 cost to increase; FY28 revenue growth guidance deferred to later calls.
Depreciation step-up from new capacity is weighing on PAT (6.8% margin vs 10.5%).
key_quotes: We see this moderation in margins as a temporary blip rather than a structural deterioration and continue to maintain our focus on volume-led market share growth.
However, visibility on margin guidance remains limited owing to abrupt fluctuation in raw material prices.

So, it's a choice that we've taken that during this time, only for a near-term margin consideration, we don't want to increase the price but become a little more aggressive to ensure that long-term benefits to the company are received in terms of higher shelf space in the retail counters.
So, if the prices continue to be at this level, then that is the increase that we might have to take to ensure that our margins for FY28 to reach back to our targeted range of 16-odd percent.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term margins, but cautious and evasive on near-term margin visibility and FY28 guidance, which management repeatedly tied to raw material price volatility. Management framed the margin dip as a temporary choice to prioritise volume and market share.
